problem: The sentence after 'Three series cover most exam problems' is garbled: 'As a numeric identity they need |x|3.2.' It is unreadable and the condition is incomplete, so a student cannot tell when the series formulas are valid as numbers.
fix: As numeric identities, 1/(1−x) = Σxⁿ needs |x| < 1, and 1/(1−ax) = Σaⁿxⁿ needs |ax| < 1. The binomial series (1+x)ⁿ = Σ C(n,k)x^k is a finite sum, so it always holds. As formal power series, none of them needs any condition on x.

problem: The symbol b in h_n = Σ_{k=0}^{n} a_k b_{n−k} is never defined. Only a_n has been introduced, and the formula block lists just a, C(n,k) and n.
fix: Add: b_k is the coefficient of x^k in F(x), that is F(x) = Σ_{k≥0} b_k x^k, and a_k = [x^k]G(x).

problem: The partial-fraction recipe 'write the fraction as A/(1−αx)+B/(1−βx)+⋯' silently assumes the fraction is proper and that Q(0) ≠ 0. A student who meets P of degree ≥ deg Q, or a factor x in Q, will get stuck.
fix: Add: first divide P by Q if deg P ≥ deg Q, and keep only the remainder over Q; also Q must have Q(0) ≠ 0 so that every factor can be written as (1−αx); if not, take out a power of x first.

problem: The remark 'Some syllabi call this simply the generating function' appears twice, in the lead and again in Section 1, which reads as repetition.
fix: Keep it once, preferably in Section 1 where the OGF is defined.

problem: 'adding, shifting and multiplying sequences become algebra on polynomials' is imprecise: G(x) is a power series, not a polynomial, and the point of the chapter is that infinite series behave like polynomials here.
fix: Write 'become algebra on power series, done the way you handle polynomials'.
